**Bare `except Exception: pass` silently swallows all errors** The intent of this block appears to be to ignore duplicate-key constraint violations, but the current `except Exception: pass` also silently swallows connection failures, schema mismatches, permission errors, and any other database error. The caller (and the HTTP response) will receive `{"totalIndexed": N}` even when every single insert has failed, giving the impression that indexing succeeded when it did not. **Re-indexing accumulates duplicate entries and corrupts scores** `index_data` only ever *appends* new rows to the index table; it never deletes existing entries for the target model(s) before inserting. This means that every time the indexing endpoint (or the programmatic function) is called for the same model, all its tokens are written to the index a second (third, …) time. The direct consequence is broken scoring: `search_index` aggregates by incrementing `entry["score"]` once per matching row. After two indexing runs, each token match appears twice, so every record's score doubles — effectively destroying ranking correctness for any reindex scenario. Before starting the per-model insert loop, the existing entries for that model should be deleted: ```python # At the start of each model iteration: await db.delete_many(index_table, {"model": model_name}) ``` (The exact DataFn API for bulk deletion may differ; adjust to match the adapter's interface.)
